1	# Hack Western 13 handoff v2: AI Robot Redesign Engine
2	
3	Updated Sat Nov 21, 2026. Devpost deadline: **Sun Nov 22, 9am EST**.
4	
5	**What changed from v1:** we no longer just recommend US-made replacement parts. We **find a replacement, check that it works, and regenerate the robot's CAD to fit it.** The sourcing and compliance work from v1 becomes step 1 ("why this part has to go").
6	
7	**Still valid in [HANDOFF.md](HANDOFF.md) (v1):** policy facts and sources (§2), prize rules and how to compete for each track (§3, §3a), TinyFish limits (§4), rejected ideas (§8). [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) describes the v1 design. Where it disagrees with this file, this file wins.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 1. The pitch
12	
13	> "This robot's drive motor has to be replaced to meet US sourcing rules. Finding another motor is easy. The hard part is knowing it actually works and changing the robot to fit it. Our AI engineer does both, live."
14	
15	**Hackathon scope:** a small wheeled robot. **One subsystem, the drive motor and its mounting bracket**, is redesigned end to end. Then we generate 2–3 competing designs (lowest cost, best performance, US-first).
16	
17	**Full product vision (pitch only, don't build):** upload any CAD assembly and BOM, redesign every affected subsystem, run simulation, and export for engineering review.
18	
19	---
20	
21	## 2. Simplifications (locked, don't reopen)
22	
23	1. **NEMA-standard motors only (NEMA 17 / 23 / 34).** The frame size fixes the bolt pattern, pilot diameter and shaft diameter. The agent only has to find **frame size, body length, torque, speed and voltage**, which are usually plain text on the page. Bolt patterns come from our lookup table (§6), not from Gemini reading drawings.
24	2. **We build the whole robot ourselves in CadQuery:** base plate, wheels, motor mounts, electronics box. Don't import GrabCAD models (painful to convert, license restrictions, not parametric). Clean and labelled is better than realistic.
25	3. **Parametric template, not general CAD editing.** The bracket is a function `bracket(frame, body_len, clearance)`. Be upfront about this in the pitch.
26	4. **One subsystem.** We show the whole robot, but only the motor mount changes.
27	5. **Four checks, all in code:** torque, speed, voltage and fit (§6). "Pass" means "passes the checks we implemented", and the UI says so.
28	
29	---
30	
31	## 3. Fixes from review (build these into the design)
32	
33	1. **Magnets are a supply risk, not a compliance hit.** My understanding of the Buy American Act component test (confirm with counsel before saying it on stage): a component is domestic if *it* is made in the US, whatever its sub-parts (except iron and steel). A US-made motor with Chinese NdFeB magnets still counts as domestic. **Show two separate tracks:** "Compliance: 67% ✅" and "Supply risk: magnets ⚠️". Never mix them.
34	2. **US final assembly is required too.** A robot is a "domestic end product" only if it is **manufactured in the US** *and* more than 65% of its component cost is domestic. If the demo robot is Canadian-built, the verdict must say "also needs US final assembly." Canadian parts count as foreign.
35	3. **Every swap gets a fit badge:** `drop_in` / `close` / `needs_review`, with a spec comparison table (for example "torque 0.28 vs 0.30 Nm (−7%)"). The code checks decide pass or fail. Gemini only writes the explanation.
36	4. **Concurrency fallback for the live tiles.** A standard account gets about 2 Agent runs at a time. Ask the TinyFish booth for an increase first thing. If we don't get it: run TinyBrowser sessions (5) plus cached replays, and say in the pitch which tiles are live.
37	5. **Build order.** Core first, in this order: **robot CAD + bracket generator → agents find real motors → checks → regenerated bracket in the viewer.** Nothing else until that works end to end.
38	
39	---
40	
41	## 4. Making the TinyFish part strong
42	
43	TinyFish judges on: **a real job done start to finish, agents that hold up on live websites, smart use of TinyFish, and a demo that makes them want to hire it.** The CAD step is what the job *produces*. It doesn't replace the job. Present it like a job description:
44	
45	> **Role:** Sourcing engineer. **Each run:** searches US motor manufacturers and distributors, reads product pages and datasheets, verifies origin and price from the source, and delivers specs that the CAD engine can build from.
46	
47	| Step | TinyFish product | What it does |
48	|---|---|---|
49	| Discovery | **TinySearch** + **TinyFetch** (free within limits) | Broad search across manufacturers and distributors for NEMA motors that meet the requirements. Cheap, so cast a wide net. |
50	| Deep extraction | **TinyAgent** (`/run-batch`, `/run-sse`) | Opens product pages, finds the datasheet, and returns the `output_schema` below. **Shows `streaming_url` tiles live on screen.** |
51	| Verification | **TinyFetch** (`html`) | Fetches the source page again and checks in code that `origin_quote`, the price and the frame size appear word for word. |
52	| Quote flow | **TinyBrowser** + Playwright | Fills one supplier's RFQ or quote form and **stops before submitting**. That's the end-to-end "job done." |
53	| Watching | **TinyMonitor** | Watches the chosen motor's page for price or stock changes. Events go to Tiger Data. |
54	
55	**Rules that make it hold up:**
56	- Every result carries `status` + `reason`. `COMPLETED` does not mean success.
57	- Data fields are optional, so unreachable fields don't get placeholder values.
58	- Use `max_duration_seconds` (GA) as the run limit. `max_steps` needs beta access.
59	- No CAPTCHA solving: mark the site `blocked` and move on. Test target sites in hour one.
60	- One honest identity on real sites. No fake personas.
61	- **Log every run to Tiger Data** (§8), then show a "success rate by site" panel. That's evidence the agents hold up on live websites, not just a claim.
62	- Pre-identify 2–3 real NEMA motors that the swarm is known to find, so the demo can't come up empty.
63	
64	**`output_schema` for the agent:**
65	
66	```json
67	{
68	  "status": "success | blocked | not_found | auth_required | incomplete",
69	  "reason": "string",
70	  "manufacturer": "string?",
71	  "part_number": "string?",
72	  "nema_frame": "string? (17 | 23 | 34)",
73	  "body_length_mm": "number?",
74	  "rated_torque_nm": "number?",
75	  "rated_speed_rpm": "number?",
76	  "voltage_v": "number?",
77	  "shaft_diameter_mm": "number?",
78	  "price_usd": "number?",
79	  "lead_time_days": "number?",
80	  "country_of_origin": "string?",
81	  "origin_quote": "string? (exact text from the page)",
82	  "product_url": "string?",
83	  "datasheet_url": "string?"
84	}
85	```
86	
87	**Social post (required for eligibility):** post the demo clip on X or LinkedIn and tag TinyFish.
88	
89	---
90	
91	## 5. Pipeline: who does what
92	
93	| # | Step | Done by |
94	|---|---|---|
95	| 1 | Load the robot (parametric CadQuery model + BOM + requirements) | Code |
96	| 2 | Compliance card: coverage check, domestic %, US-assembly requirement, magnet supply-risk flag | Code |
97	| 3 | Plan the search: requirements → queries + target sites | Gemini |
98	| 4 | Discovery + extraction | TinyFish |
99	| 5 | Read datasheet PDFs where the page lacks specs | Gemini (multimodal, strict JSON) |
100	| 6 | Verify origin, price and frame size against the page HTML | Code |
101	| 7 | Engineering checks: torque, speed, voltage, fit | Code |
102	| 8 | Tournament: choose the best candidate by cost / performance / US-first | Code |
103	| 9 | Regenerate the bracket + assembly, export GLB | Code (CadQuery) |
104	| 10 | Explanations, comparison write-up, RFQ draft | Gemini (numbers passed in, no math) |
105	
106	**Hard rules:** the LLM never does arithmetic. Every number links to its source. Unverified candidates never reach the checks. "Not legal advice / not engineering certification" stays visible in the UI.
107	
108	---
109	
110	## 6. Engineering checks (code)
111	
112	Inputs from the robot's spec: mass `m`, wheel radius `r`, number of drive motors `n`, gear ratio `G`, drivetrain efficiency `η`, rolling resistance `Crr`, maximum slope `θ`, target acceleration `a`, top speed `v_max`, bus voltage `V_bus`, safety factor `SF` (about 1.5).
113	
114	| Check | Pass if |
115	|---|---|
116	| Torque | `r·m·(g·(Crr·cosθ + sinθ) + a) / (n·G·η) · SF ≤ rated_torque_nm` |
117	| Speed | `(rated_speed_rpm / G) · 2πr / 60 ≥ v_max` |
118	| Voltage | `voltage_v` matches `V_bus` (or is within the driver's supported range) |
119	| Fit | `body_length_mm + bracket thickness + clearance ≤ chassis envelope`, and `nema_frame` is in the lookup table |
120	
121	Result per candidate: **Rejected** (fails torque, speed or voltage), **Review** (fits only with changes, or data is missing), **Pass\*** (meets every check we implemented).
122	
123	**NEMA lookup table.** These are typical values. **Check each one against a real vendor drawing before building**, because shaft size varies by model.
124	
125	| Frame | Bolt-hole spacing (square) | Pilot diameter | Common shaft diameter |
126	|---|---|---|---|
127	| NEMA 17 | 31.0 mm | 22.0 mm | 5 mm |
128	| NEMA 23 | 47.14 mm | 38.1 mm | 6.35 mm or 8 mm |
129	| NEMA 34 | 69.6 mm | 73.0 mm | 9.5 / 12.7 / 14 mm |
130	
131	---
132	
133	## 7. CAD engine
134	
135	- **CadQuery** (Python). Functions: `robot(params)`, `motor(frame, body_len)`, `bracket(frame, body_len, clearance)`.
136	- The bracket uses the bolt spacing and pilot diameter from the NEMA table, its width comes from the frame size, and its depth and position move with `body_len`.
137	- Export the assembly to **GLB** (glTF) for the browser, and to **STEP** as the "engineering export".
138	- Viewer: **`<model-viewer>`** or **three.js** with a **before/after slider**, the changed bracket highlighted, and the three tournament designs as tabs.
139	- **Start this first.** It's the least familiar piece and the biggest moment in the demo.
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 8. Sponsor technology: how each one is used
144	
145	### TinyFish (core prize)
146	See §4. Search/Fetch for discovery, Agent for extraction with live tiles, Fetch HTML for verification, Browser for the RFQ form, Monitor for price and stock changes.
147	
148	### Gemini (MLH Best Use of Gemini)
149	- **Multimodal datasheet reading:** send PDFs or images of spec tables directly and get back **strict JSON** that matches our motor schema.
150	- **Long context:** compare 3–5 candidate datasheets side by side in one call and produce the spec comparison text.
151	- **Search planning:** robot requirements → search queries + target sites for TinyFish.
152	- **Writing:** fit explanations ("why Motor B needs review"), the design comparison write-up, and the RFQ draft.
153	- **Deliberately not used for:** arithmetic, pass/fail decisions, origin verification. Say this in the Devpost write-up.
154	
155	### Vultr (MLH Best Use of Vultr)
156	- **Backend on Vultr compute:** orchestrator API (FastAPI) + workers. Put CadQuery (OCCT dependencies) in a Docker image on the Vultr VM so nobody fights local installs.
157	- **Tournament in parallel:** each design variant is a worker job (checks + CAD regeneration + GLB export) running at the same time.
158	- **Vultr Object Storage** (S3-compatible): generated GLB/STEP files, downloaded datasheets, and captured HTML evidence for the verifier.
159	- Show the architecture diagram in the demo and name Vultr.
160	
161	### Tiger Data (MLH Best Use of Tiger Data)
162	Real time-series use, not just tables:
163	- **`agent_runs`** (hypertable): `time, run_id, site, product, status, duration_s, steps`. Continuous aggregate **`site_success_hourly`** powers the "success rate by site" panel. That panel doubles as TinyFish evidence.
164	- **`price_observations`** (hypertable): `time, part_number, supplier, price_usd, lead_time_days, origin, run_id`. Filled by repeated runs and TinyMonitor events.
165	- **`check_results`** (hypertable): `time, design_id, candidate, check, value, threshold, pass`. This is the audit trail behind each Pass/Review/Rejected.
166	- **`design_variants`** (regular table, same database): design ID, objective, cost, domestic %, GLB URL. Relational and time-series data side by side is Tiger Data's pitch.
167	- Name the hypertables and continuous aggregates in the Devpost write-up.
168	
169	### Also cheap to add (details in v1 §3a)
170	- **Auth0:** a manager approves before the RFQ is submitted.
171	- **Entire:** one Trail per feature plus session handoffs (see [ENTIRE.md](ENTIRE.md)).
172	- **GoDaddy:** a live domain hosting the demo.
173	
174	---
175	
176	## 9. Demo script (3 minutes)
177	
178	1. **The problem (20 s):** the robot in 3D. "This drive motor has to go: here's the compliance card." It shows 38% domestic, needs US final assembly, and a separate magnet supply-risk flag.
179	2. **Find and Redesign (60 s):** click. Live TinyFish tiles search manufacturers and distributors, and verified results pop in (✅ / ⚠️ blocked / ❌ not found).
180	3. **Engineering checks (30 s):** the table shows Motor A Rejected (torque), Motor B Review (fit), Motor C Pass\*. Each number links to its source.
181	4. **The key moment (40 s):** the bracket regenerates. Before/after slider: the bracket widens and the holes move. STEP export button.
182	5. **Tournament (20 s):** three tabs (lowest cost / best performance / US-first), each with its cost, domestic %, and 3D model.
183	6. **Close (10 s):** RFQ drafted and waiting for approval. "From 'this part has to go' to a buildable design in 3 minutes."
184	
185	---
186	
187	## 10. Team split
188	
189	| Owner | Area |
190	|---|---|
191	| 1 | **CAD:** parametric robot + bracket in CadQuery, GLB/STEP export, 3D viewer with before/after |
192	| 2 | **Agents:** TinyFish discovery/extraction/verification, Gemini datasheet extraction, run logging |
193	| 3 | **Engineering + data:** checks, NEMA table, demo robot requirements, compliance card, 2–3 pre-identified real motors, Tiger Data schema |
194	| 4 | **Frontend + infra + demo:** UI flow, live tiles, comparison view, Vultr deployment, domain, video, social post |
195	
196	## 11. Milestones
197	
198	- [ ] **Now:** TinyFish booth (concurrency increase, beta access for `max_steps`, file upload). Ask the organizers about prize stacking. Test target sites for bot walls.
199	- [ ] **Sat 2pm:** a bracket regenerates from hard-coded motor specs and shows up in the viewer.
200	- [ ] **Sat 6pm:** the swarm returns verified specs for at least 2 real motors. The checks give Pass/Review/Rejected.
201	- [ ] **Sat 10pm:** end to end: click → agents → checks → regenerated bracket. Deployed on Vultr.
202	- [ ] **Sun 2am:** tournament (3 variants), Tiger Data panels, RFQ draft.
203	- [ ] **Sun 4am: FEATURE FREEZE.** 4–8am: pre-run and cache demo inputs, record a backup video, write the Devpost page, post the social clip.
204	
205	## 12. What to cut if we're behind (cut first at the top)
206	
207	1. Auth0 approval → show the RFQ as a draft only
208	2. TinyMonitor → static price history
209	3. Tournament → one redesign only
210	4. TinyBrowser quote form → link to the supplier's quote page
211	5. Tiger Data panels → a basic table (Tiger Data keeps logging in the background)
212	
213	**Never cut:** live agents finding real motors, code-based checks, the regenerated bracket in the viewer.

1	# Architecture
2	
3	How the AI Robot Redesign Engine is put together. For the plan, demo script, milestones and team split, see [HANDOFF-v2.md](HANDOFF-v2.md). For policy facts, prize rules and TinyFish limits, see [HANDOFF.md](HANDOFF.md) (v1). For Entire commands, see [ENTIRE.md](ENTIRE.md).
4	
5	## 1. Overview
6	
7	An engineer has a robot whose drive motor must be replaced to meet US sourcing rules. The system:
8	
9	1. shows **why** the part has to go: a compliance card (FCC coverage, domestic-content % against the 65% and 75% lines, the US final-assembly requirement) and a **separate** supply-risk flag (for example NdFeB magnets)
10	2. sends a **TinyFish agent swarm** to find real NEMA-frame replacement motors on live manufacturer and distributor websites, extract their specs, and verify origin and price against the source page
11	3. runs **deterministic engineering checks** (torque, speed, voltage, fit) and labels each candidate Rejected / Review / Pass\*
12	4. **regenerates the robot's CAD** in CadQuery: a new motor mounting bracket sized to the chosen motor, exported as GLB for the browser and STEP for engineers
13	5. runs a small **tournament** of 2–3 designs (lowest cost, best performance, US-first) and shows them side by side in 3D
14	6. drafts an RFQ for the chosen supplier and holds it for approval
15	
16	Hackathon scope: one small wheeled robot that we model ourselves, and one subsystem (drive motor + bracket). This is a parametric template, not general editing of uploaded CAD files.
17	
18	## 2. Diagram
19	
20	```mermaid
21	flowchart LR
22	  U[Engineer] -->|robot params, BOM, requirements| API
23	
24	  subgraph Vultr[Vultr compute]
25	    API[Orchestrator API] --> CMP[Compliance card]
26	    API --> PLAN[Search planner]
27	    PLAN --> SW[Agent swarm]
28	    SW --> VF[Verifier]
29	    VF --> CHK[Engineering checks]
30	    CHK --> TRN[Tournament]
31	    TRN --> CAD[CAD workers: CadQuery]
32	  end
33	
34	  PLAN -->|requirements| GEM[Gemini]
35	  SW <-->|TinySearch, TinyFetch, TinyAgent| WEB[(Manufacturer and distributor sites)]
36	  SW -->|datasheet PDFs| GEM
37	  VF -->|re-fetch html, string-match| WEB
38	  MON[TinyMonitor: chosen motor page] -->|price, stock changes| TS
39	
40	  CAD -->|GLB, STEP| OBJ[(Vultr Object Storage)]
41	  VF -->|html evidence| OBJ
42	
43	  SW & CHK -->|runs, prices, check results| TS[(Tiger Data)]
44	
45	  TRN --> RFQ[RFQ draft: Gemini]
46	  RFQ -->|TinyBrowser fills form, stops before submit| A0[Auth0: manager approves]
47	
48	  OBJ --> FE[Frontend: 3D viewer, live tiles, comparison]
49	  TS --> FE
50	  CMP --> FE
51	```
52	
53	## 3. Components
54	
55	| # | Component | What it does | Deterministic or LLM | Owner |
56	|---|---|---|---|---|
57	| 1 | Robot model | Parametric CadQuery robot (base plate, wheels, motor mounts, electronics box) plus its BOM and requirements (mass, wheel radius, gear ratio, top speed, bus voltage, chassis envelope). | Deterministic | CAD |
58	| 2 | Compliance card | Checks FCC coverage, computes domestic % by component cost (unknown origin = foreign), shows the US final-assembly requirement, and flags supply risks on a separate track. | Deterministic | Engineering + data |
59	| 3 | Search planner | Turns the motor requirements into search queries and target sites. Seeded with 2–3 pre-identified real motors. | Gemini | Agents |
60	| 4 | Agent swarm | TinySearch + TinyFetch for broad discovery; TinyAgent for product pages and datasheets, returning the motor `output_schema`; live `streaming_url` tiles. | TinyFish | Agents |
61	| 5 | Datasheet reader | Reads datasheet PDFs and spec-table images when the product page lacks specs, and returns strict JSON. | Gemini (multimodal) | Agents |
62	| 6 | Verifier | Fetches the source page again and string-matches origin, price and NEMA frame against the html. Saves the html as evidence. | Deterministic | Agents |
63	| 7 | Engineering checks | Torque, speed, voltage and fit checks (§5) give Rejected / Review / Pass\*, plus a fit badge (`drop_in` / `close` / `needs_review`) and a spec comparison table. | Deterministic | Engineering + data |
64	| 8 | Tournament | Picks the best passing candidate for each objective: lowest cost, best performance, US-first. | Deterministic | Engineering + data |
65	| 9 | CAD workers | Regenerate the bracket and assembly for each design using the NEMA lookup table, then export GLB and STEP. One job per design, run in parallel. | Deterministic (CadQuery) | CAD |
66	| 10 | Writer | Fit explanations, the design comparison write-up and the RFQ draft. Numbers are passed in, never computed. | Gemini | Agents |
67	| 11 | RFQ flow | TinyBrowser + Playwright fills one supplier's quote form and stops before submitting. Auth0 approval is required to send. | TinyFish + Auth0 | Agents |
68	| 12 | Frontend | Compliance card, live agent tiles, check results table, 3D viewer with before/after slider, design tabs, Tiger Data panels. | n/a | Frontend + infra |
69	
70	## 4. Data flow and schemas
71	
72	**Robot requirements (input)**
73	
74	| Field | Type | Notes |
75	|---|---|---|
76	| `mass_kg` | number | robot mass including payload |
77	| `wheel_radius_m` | number | |
78	| `n_drive_motors` | int | |
79	| `gear_ratio` | number | `G` |
80	| `efficiency` | number | drivetrain `η` |
81	| `crr` | number | rolling resistance |
82	| `max_slope_deg` | number | `θ` |
83	| `accel_mps2` | number | target acceleration `a` |
84	| `v_max_mps` | number | top speed |
85	| `bus_voltage_v` | number | |
86	| `envelope_mm` | number | space available for motor + bracket |
87	| `safety_factor` | number | about 1.5 |
88	
89	**BOM row (input)**
90	
91	| Field | Type | Notes |
92	|---|---|---|
93	| `part` | string | |
94	| `category` | string | motor, gearbox, encoder, battery, compute, sensor, frame and so on |
95	| `qty` | int | |
96	| `unit_cost_usd` | decimal | |
97	| `origin` | ISO country code or `unknown` | `unknown` counts as foreign; Canadian parts count as foreign |
98	| `supply_risk` | string? | for example `ndfeb_magnets`. Shown separately; does not change domestic % |
99	
100	**Agent `output_schema` (one per candidate motor)**
101	
102	A run that reports `COMPLETED` has not necessarily met its goal, so every result carries its own status. Data fields are optional so the agent doesn't fill unreachable ones with placeholders.
103	
104	```json
105	{
106	  "status": "success | blocked | not_found | auth_required | incomplete",
107	  "reason": "string",
108	  "manufacturer": "string?",
109	  "part_number": "string?",
110	  "nema_frame": "string? (17 | 23 | 34)",
111	  "body_length_mm": "number?",
112	  "rated_torque_nm": "number?",
113	  "rated_speed_rpm": "number?",
114	  "voltage_v": "number?",
115	  "shaft_diameter_mm": "number?",
116	  "price_usd": "number?",
117	  "lead_time_days": "number?",
118	  "country_of_origin": "string?",
119	  "origin_quote": "string? (exact text from the page)",
120	  "product_url": "string?",
121	  "datasheet_url": "string?"
122	}
123	```
124	
125	**Verifier statuses:** `verified`, `price_mismatch`, `origin_not_found`, `frame_mismatch`, `blocked`, `rejected`. Only `verified` candidates reach the engineering checks.
126	
127	**Check result (per candidate):** `verdict` (`rejected | review | pass`), `fit` (`drop_in | close | needs_review`), and one row per check with `value`, `threshold`, `pass` and source links.
128	
129	**Design variant (per tournament entry):** `design_id`, `objective` (`cost | performance | us_first`), `motor` (part number), `cost_usd`, `domestic_pct`, `glb_url`, `step_url`.
130	
131	**Tiger Data**
132	
133	- `agent_runs` (hypertable): `time`, `run_id`, `site`, `product`, `status`, `duration_s`, `steps`.
134	- `site_success_hourly` (continuous aggregate over `agent_runs`): powers the "success rate by site" panel, which is also evidence that the agents hold up on live websites.
135	- `price_observations` (hypertable): `time`, `part_number`, `supplier`, `price_usd`, `lead_time_days`, `origin`, `run_id`. Filled by repeated runs and TinyMonitor events.
136	- `check_results` (hypertable): `time`, `design_id`, `candidate`, `check`, `value`, `threshold`, `pass`. The audit trail behind each verdict.
137	- `design_variants` (regular table in the same database): the design variant fields above.
138	
139	## 5. Engineering checks and CAD
140	
141	**Checks** (all code; symbols from the requirements table):
142	
143	| Check | Pass if |
144	|---|---|
145	| Torque | `r·m·(g·(Crr·cosθ + sinθ) + a) / (n·G·η) · SF ≤ rated_torque_nm` |
146	| Speed | `(rated_speed_rpm / G) · 2πr / 60 ≥ v_max` |
147	| Voltage | `voltage_v` matches `bus_voltage_v` (or is within the driver's supported range) |
148	| Fit | `body_length_mm + bracket thickness + clearance ≤ envelope_mm`, and `nema_frame` is in the lookup table |
149	
150	**NEMA lookup table.** Typical values. Check each one against a real vendor drawing before building.
151	
152	| Frame | Bolt-hole spacing (square) | Pilot diameter | Common shaft diameter |
153	|---|---|---|---|
154	| NEMA 17 | 31.0 mm | 22.0 mm | 5 mm |
155	| NEMA 23 | 47.14 mm | 38.1 mm | 6.35 mm or 8 mm |
156	| NEMA 34 | 69.6 mm | 73.0 mm | 9.5 / 12.7 / 14 mm |
157	
158	**CAD functions** (CadQuery):
159	
160	- `robot(params)`: the full assembly
161	- `motor(frame, body_len)`: a simple motor body from the NEMA table
162	- `bracket(frame, body_len, clearance)`: bolt spacing and pilot hole from the NEMA table; width from the frame; depth and position from `body_len`
163	
164	Export: `cq.Assembly` to **GLB** for the viewer and **STEP** for the engineering export. The viewer (`<model-viewer>` or three.js) highlights the changed bracket and has a before/after slider.
165	
166	## 6. Hard rules
167	
168	1. The LLM never does arithmetic. All costs, percentages, checks and optimization are plain code.
169	2. Pass/fail comes from code checks and documented specs, never from an LLM's judgment.
170	3. Unknown origin counts as foreign. Allied content does not count, so Canadian parts are foreign.
171	4. Compliance and supply risk are separate. A US-made motor with foreign magnets still counts as domestic under the component test (confirm with counsel before stating it on stage).
172	5. A domestic end product must also be manufactured in the US. The compliance card says so whenever the robot is built elsewhere.
173	6. Every number in the UI links to its source. Nothing unverified reaches the checks.
174	7. Bolt patterns come from the NEMA lookup table, not from an LLM reading drawings.
175	8. No RFQ is submitted without Auth0 approval. One honest identity on real vendor sites; no fake personas.
176	9. The UI says "not legal advice" and "Pass\* = passes the checks we implemented, not engineering certification". The COTS question is shown as "flag for counsel".
177	10. No API keys or TinyFish credentials in prompts, because Entire session transcripts are pushed with the code.
178	
179	## 7. Where each sponsor fits
180	
181	| Sponsor | Where it runs | Where it is deliberately not used |
182	|---|---|---|
183	| TinyFish | TinySearch + TinyFetch for discovery; TinyAgent for product pages and datasheets with live tiles; TinyFetch html for verification; TinyBrowser for the RFQ form; TinyMonitor on the chosen motor's page | Broad discovery doesn't use Agent runs (cost and concurrency) |
184	| Gemini | Search planning; multimodal datasheet reading with strict JSON; long-context comparison of 3–5 datasheets; fit explanations, comparison write-up, RFQ draft | Arithmetic, pass/fail verdicts, origin verification, bolt patterns |
185	| Vultr | Orchestrator API (FastAPI) and workers in Docker (CadQuery/OCCT image); tournament designs as parallel CAD jobs; Object Storage for GLB/STEP files, datasheets and html evidence | n/a |
186	| Tiger Data | Hypertables for agent runs, prices and check results; continuous aggregate for site success rate; relational `design_variants` in the same database | n/a |
187	| Auth0 | Auth0 for AI Agents: manager approval before the RFQ is submitted; roles (engineer drafts, manager approves) | n/a |
188	| Entire | Trails per feature with review agents, overnight session handoffs, Brain for key decisions, graph search with measured token savings | n/a |
189	| GoDaddy | Live domain hosting the demo | n/a |
190	
191	## 8. Limits and fallbacks
192	
193	| Limit | How we handle it |
194	|---|---|
195	| About 2 concurrent TinyFish Agent runs and 5 Browser sessions on standard accounts | Queue runs with `/run-batch`. Ask the booth for a hackathon increase. Otherwise fill the tile wall with Browser sessions and cached replays, and say which tiles are live. |
196	| No CAPTCHA solving | Mark the site `blocked` and move on. Prefer sites with no bot wall (test in hour one). |
197	| `max_steps` needs beta access | Use `max_duration_seconds` (GA) as the run limit. |
198	| No screenshots | Store the captured `html` as evidence and use it for the verifier string-match. |
199	| File upload in TinyAgent is unclear | Use TinyBrowser + Playwright `setInputFiles`. |
200	| Datasheet dimensions misread | Only frame size, body length and ratings come from the web; bolt patterns come from the NEMA table. Mismatches go to Review. |
201	| The swarm comes up empty on demo day | 2–3 real motors are pre-identified and seeded into the planner. |
202	| CadQuery install pain | Run it in a Docker image on Vultr, so nobody installs OCCT locally. |
203	| Live websites fail during the demo | Pre-run and cache demo inputs; record a backup video. |
204	
205	## 9. Repo layout
206	
207	> **Stub:** fill in once the stack is chosen. One folder per owner from the team split in HANDOFF-v2.md:
208	>
209	> 1. CAD: parametric robot, bracket generator, GLB/STEP export, viewer
210	> 2. Agents: TinyFish swarm, datasheet reader, verifier, RFQ flow
211	> 3. Engineering + data: checks, tournament, NEMA table, compliance card, demo robot requirements, Tiger Data schema
212	> 4. Frontend + infra: UI, live tiles, comparison view, Vultr deployment

I'd build the demo around one swap: the robot's cheap imported NEMA 17 stepper becomes a US-made NEMA 23 Teknic ClearPath servo.

That swap gives you the biggest visible change in the bracket. The bolt pattern grows from 31 mm to 47.14 mm, the pilot hole from 22 mm to 38.1 mm, and the motor body roughly doubles in length. It also matches the pitch: the drop-in replacement fails, and the one that works needs new CAD.

## The "before" robot

Build our own CadQuery robot rather than importing anyone's CAD, as §2 of the handoff says.

| Parameter | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Drive | 2 motors, differential, belt reduction G = 4 | |
| Mass `m` | 12 kg | |
| Wheel radius `r` | 50 mm | |
| Efficiency η, Crr, slope θ, accel `a` | 0.9, 0.03, 10°, 0.5 m/s² | |
| `v_max` | 1.0 m/s | Motor must reach about 764 rpm |
| Bus voltage | 24 V | |
| Safety factor | 1.5 | |
| Envelope | 125 mm | Picked so a 110 mm motor fits and a 123–129 mm one doesn't |

With these numbers the §6 torque formula requires about **0.31 Nm**. I worked that by hand, so re-run it in code. The original motor fits this robot.

**Original motor ("has to go"):** a generic NEMA 17 like the [ZYLtech 0.42 Nm stepper](https://www.zyltech.com/nema-17-stepper-motor-1-5-a-0-42-nm-59-ozin-1-3-or-5-pack/). It costs about $15 and passes the 0.31 Nm requirement. Its page gives no country of origin, so under our rule (unknown counts as foreign) it lands as foreign on the compliance card.

## Three candidates for the checks table

| Slot | Motor | Specs (from Teknic's own model pages) | Expected result |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | A short NEMA 17 found by the swarm | Holding torque under 0.31 Nm | **Rejected (torque).** It would bolt straight on, but it's too weak. |
| **B** | [Teknic CPM-SDHP-2336F-ELS](https://teknic.com/model-info/CPM-SDHP-2336F-ELS) | NEMA 23, 129.29 mm long, 465 oz-in, 5300 rpm, 24–75 VDC | **Review (fit).** 129 mm plus bracket and clearance exceeds the 125 mm envelope. |
| **C** | [Teknic CPM-IPSK-2321H-RQNB](https://teknic.com/model-info/CPM-IPSK-2321H-RQNB) | NEMA 23, 110.24 mm long, 492 oz-in, 3240 rpm, 24–75 VDC | **Pass\*.** The bracket regenerates for NEMA 23. |

For the tournament tabs:
- **Lowest cost:** a US-made NEMA 17, if the swarm finds one strong enough.
- **US-first:** Teknic C.
- **Best performance:** a Teknic NEMA 34. The bracket becomes huge and probably goes to Review on fit, which is still a good visual.

## Check these before building on them

1. **Teknic's origin wording.** Teknic is in Victor, NY, but I haven't found an exact "made in USA" line on a product page yet. The verifier needs that exact text in `origin_quote`, so someone should find it.
2. **Peak vs continuous torque.** The 465 and 492 oz-in figures from the search results may be peak torque. Use the continuous rating in the torque check.
3. **The model-info pages are hard to scrape.** I fetched the two Teknic pages with TinyFetch in markdown and got only the feature boilerplate, not the spec table. So the extraction step needs TinyAgent or TinyFetch with `format: html`. That actually helps the pitch for why we use TinyAgent. Test it in hour one.
4. **Voltage check for steppers.** The ZYLtech page says "Rated Voltage (≠driving voltage): 2.4V". A stepper's rated voltage isn't the bus voltage, so compare it against the driver's supported range instead.
5. **Slot A is still open.** I couldn't confirm a real US-made NEMA 17. Possible sources are Lin Engineering, Haydon Kerk and Applied Motion. If none is US-made, Slot A can be any weak NEMA 17 and still show the torque rejection.
6. **Optional realism.** If Teknic offers STEP downloads, drop the real motor body into the assembly and keep only the bracket parametric.

Once someone confirms the Teknic origin text and continuous torque, these three can be the seeded "known to find" motors from §4.
